Mini-scale tearing modes are anticipated in collisionless plasmas once the kinetic magnetic Reynolds number exceeds the critical threshold of approximately 3000. This study examines the linear instability of such modes in the regime where it exceeds this threshold. We derive the most rigorous analytical formulation of the local differential equation governing these plasmas and develop scaling laws for the growth rate and wavenumber of the unstable mode under both weak and strong obliquity. Oblique modes exhibit shorter wavelengths and a higher propensity for instability compared to purely slab modes. Through numerical simulations of the full linear equation, we validate the derived scalings and observe that the growth rate is influenced by the ratio of the background wavenumbers perpendicular and parallel to the k-y plane. Additionally, we analyze the nonlinear saturation of the mini-scale tearing mode, demonstrating that it shares the same characteristics as standard slabs tearing modes at marginal stability: magnetic reconnection generates magnetic islands that coalesce into a single dominant island, which eventually fills the simulation box. Finally, we discuss the potential for this instability to drive secondary instabilities. These findings are applicable to slabs with high magnetic Reynolds numbers in largely collisionless plasmas. This includes laboratory plasmas in high-energy density states, such as those found in laser-plasma experiments involving magnetic field generation via the Weibel instability or the magnetorotational instability. Furthermore, our results offer insights into the tearing modes of astrophysical systems, including the tearing of magnetospheres by solar wind magnetic fields and the local generation of magnetic fields in the solar chromosphere. We also address the mini-scale tearing mode in fusion plasmas, as well as in fusion-relevant fusion-fusion fusion reactor systems. Furthermore, our findings provide a framework for understanding the magnetic recombination observed in the solar chromosphere. The solar wind magnetosphere is also discussed in the context of these mini-scale tearing modes. We predict the formation of magnetic islands with a width of approximately 100 km, resulting in a magnetic reconfiguration that could be observable via ground-based optical telescopes. Finally, we explore the mini-scale tearing mode in the context of fusion plasmas. Driven by the growing demand for self-service retail, we introduce a novel approach to Fashion Image Retrieval (FIR) that utilizes domain-specific knowledge to semi-supervisedly manipulate image features. Our technique enables users to retrieve similar items or explore new ones by dragging a UI slider attached to a feature, thereby increasing or decreasing that attribute's magnitude within the feature space. To support this, we present a feature decoder, a non-linear function trained with hard constraints to map feature values to the co-existent semantic attributes of clothing items. We demonstrate how to integrate this mechanism into existing FIR models without altering the base retrieval system. Extensive experiments on a large-scale fashion dataset show that our approach facilitates intuitive user interactions to control item features and significantly surpasses baseline methods in both user studies and standard evaluation metrics. Furthermore, we find that the feature decoder enhances overall FIR performance even during end-to-end training. The code is accessible at: https://github.com/ailab-fau/feature_decoder. The dataset can be downloaded here: https://drive.google.

Identifying the gradient of highly nonlinear functions in infinite-dimensional spaces is challenging, particularly when dealing with linear ill-posed problems. We demonstrate that the dual gradient ascent (DGA) method, originally developed by Nesterov (2013) (Nesterov, T.Y. (2013) Dual averaging algorithms for variational problems. Mathematical Programming, 140(1), 275-291.) for finite-dimensional settings, can be extended to Banach spaces. We establish the convergence of this method to the Shvartzman regularization path (Shvartzman, Y. (1997) An algorithm for solving ill-posed problems in Hilbert spaces. Journal of inverse problems, 13(4), 625-634.) in $H^1$ spaces and confirm its linear convergence in specific cases. Furthermore, we illustrate the potential of dual gradient ascent for the deconvolution problem. In this application, we show that a carefully chosen regularization parameter enables the method to solve ill-posed problems efficiently within a reasonable timeframe. Finally, we present numerical results comparing our approach to existing techniques. Our algorithm is highly effective, achieving results comparable to or superior to those of current state-of-the-art ill-posed problem solvers. Additionally, it exhibits superior time complexity, particularly in high-dimensional scenarios. Keywords: Banach spaces, high-dimensional spaces, infinite-dimensional spaces, optimization, regularization, numerical methods, computation, complexity, time, high-dimensional problems, infinite-dimensional problems, Banach spaces optimization, regularization, numerical methods, computation, high-dimensional problems, infinite-dimensional problems.

The widespread adoption of Light Field (LF) cameras has enabled enhanced depth perception, yet depth reconstruction remains highly sensitive to inaccuracies. This study investigates the impact of input errors on LF depth reconstruction. We identify gathering and occlusion regions within the LF encoding structure as primary sources of error. To address this, we introduce the concept of an LF camera's maximum reliable depth range, defining it as the distance from the sensing plane where the gathering region covers at least 90% of the active sensors. This range is explicitly calculated based on the camera's specific encoding function and aperture configuration. As a proof of concept, we apply this metric to the imaged plane explication (IPE) algorithm to analyze how reconstruction accuracy varies with the object's depth. Our findings indicate that reconstruction accuracy is superior in front of the sensing plane compared to depths generated by the camera's maximum maximum depth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that Light Field Cameras (LFCs) featuring larger gathering regions possess a more reliable depth range. These results provide valuable guidance for utilizing LFCs in practical applications. The source code and datasets are accessible at https://github.com/zhenghao1992/LFCC. Additionally, a web-based demo is available at https://zhenghao1992.github.io/LFCC/ for users to explore the relationship between encoding functions, encoding variables, and occlusion regions. We hope this demo will assist researchers in better understanding the characteristics of LF encoding functions. The Python source code is also provided for those interested in reproducing our results. We look forward to these outcomes assisting users in effectively using LFCs. This study introduces bilinear formulations for the completely integrable Fokas-Lenells (FL) hierarchy and derives various formulas concerning the Hirota bilinear form. Specifically, we establish the Wronskian structure of soliton solutions, the CM method, and the Casimir method for the Fokas-Lenells equation. Additionally, we provide a multisoliton solution via the pseudotrivial solution method and construct a multisoliton solution via the rank extension technique. Finally, we explicitly demonstrate that f-type multisoliton solutions can be recovered from y-type multisoliton solutions through a type conversion matrix. These findings offer novel insights into the theory of integrable nonlinear partial differential equations. The fl1_1.fl file containing solutions to the FL equation is accessible via our GitHub repository. The accompanying video illustrates how soliton solutions evolve over time within an integrable nonlinear PDE framework. This video was generated using our software, which employs a finite difference scheme based on the method of lines. Our FL equation solver, integrated within Mathematica, utilizes this software. For details on our solver and to obtain the software, please visit our website. We welcome inquiries regarding our method. Keywords: Fokas-Lenells equation; Hirota method; Multisoliton solution; Type transformation.

Our objective is to derive various non-Riemannian gravitational actions within the first-order formalism by leveraging a holographic renormalization approach in dual theories that extend standard AdS/CFT correspondence. These actions incorporate terms involving the torsion tensor and the contraction of the Ricci tensor with the non-metricity tensor, specifically the duality between the square of the torsion tensor and the contractions of the Ricci tensor with non-metricity tensors. By quantizing a non-Riemannian action using this dual relationship, we can identify the corresponding dual theory. Furthermore, we examine several properties of these actions within an on-shell context. Finally, we explore applications involving the vacuum solutions of $R + \beta P_4$ and $R + \beta P_5$ gravity, which respectively feature torsion and non-metricity. In the $R + P_4$ framework, we demonstrate that both torsion and non-metricity vanish in the Schwarzschild case. The paper concludes with a discussion of these findings. Our ultimate goal is to expand the current understanding of non-Riemannian gravity and explore potential avenues for future research in this field. Additionally, the work includes a discussion of relevant historical context. This study forms part of the author's thesis, which addresses the search for and investigation of various non-Riemannian gravitational actions. We extend our gratitude to Prof. Miguel Escobal for his invaluable guidance and support. Non-Riemannian gravity remains a relatively nascent field, and we hope this work contributes to a deeper comprehension of it. The proliferation of IEEE 802.11n/ac/ax compliant devices has significantly impacted Home WiFi networks, degrading performance through increased channel load, which subsequently affects user experience. To address this, the IEEE has developed 802.11k/m/nax/v, enabling Access Points (APs) to advise Extenders on selecting the most suitable target AP based on real-time channel load data. This paper demonstrates how the 802.11k/v standard can mitigate performance degradation by facilitating extender association with APs that offer the optimal channel load. To achieve this, we introduce a novel metric called the Channel Load to Data Rate (CLDR) ratio, which is dynamically updated using the 802.11k standard. Our simulation results indicate that this approach outperforms existing schemes in terms of overall system performance. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed method reduces co-channel interference, thereby enhancing data rates and improving User Experience Quality (UEQ). Ultimately, this study offers a significant contribution to the 802.11k/v working group by advancing the standard's capabilities. To our knowledge, this represents the first effort to utilize 802.11k/v for extender selection based on channel load. The source code is accessible at: https://github.com/802.11k/nax-v_extender_AP_choice. Our codebase is also being contributed to the 802.11k repository to support the development of that standard. Additionally, the code is provided to the 802.11n/ac/v only AP extender selection group for their reference. We welcome any feedback or suggestions from the community.
